_about: Teaching text for Module 4 (homology modelling). The structures are real (data/homology/structures.json, from the Protein Data Bank); the model is a simplified C-alpha model made by copying the template backbone.

target.name: GluA2 N-terminal domain (rat)
target.about: The N-terminal domain (NTD) of an AMPA-type glutamate receptor subunit. AMPA receptors carry most fast excitatory signalling in the brain and are targets for drugs against epilepsy and other conditions.

approaches.text: Use the experimental structure (X-ray, cryo-EM or NMR)
Homology modelling from a related protein with a known structure
A deep-learning prediction (for example AlphaFold), then check its confidence

scenarios.text: The structure of your target is already in the Protein Data Bank at 2 Å resolution.
scenarios.why: An experimental structure is the best starting point. Models and predictions are for when there is none.

scenarios.text: No structure exists for your target, but a protein with 55% identical sequence has one.
scenarios.why: Above about 40% identity the fold is conserved, so a model built on the related structure is usually reliable in the core.

scenarios.text: No structure and no close relative exist, but you can run or download a predicted structure with per-residue confidence scores.
scenarios.why: Deep-learning predictors have changed this field. Always read the confidence (for example pLDDT) before you trust a region.

scenarios.text: You already have a good structure and want to know how a flexible loop moves over microseconds.
scenarios.why: Molecular dynamics follows motion over time. It needs a good starting structure and does not create one.

reasons.text: Highest sequence identity with the target
Covers (aligns with) almost the whole target sequence
Better experimental resolution (a smaller number is better)
Is the same kind of protein in a suitable state (for example the form you want)
It has the most famous name

align.hint: Gaps inside a helix or a strand are almost always wrong. A gap belongs in a loop.

uses.text: Judge the overall fold and plan mutagenesis experiments
uses.needs: A correct fold. About 30% identity or more is usually enough.

uses.text: Dock small molecules into a binding pocket
uses.needs: An accurate pocket: high identity in the pocket (about 50% or more), correct side chains and a good alignment there. Check the pocket residues one by one.

uses.text: Replace an experimental structure in a regulatory submission
uses.needs: Not acceptable. A model is a hypothesis to be tested.

nextSteps.text: Compare with other models (other templates, a deep-learning prediction) and look at where they disagree.
Refine the model (energy minimisation or short molecular dynamics) and check it again.
Test the model with experiments, for example mutate predicted key residues and measure the effect.
Treat the model as an experimental structure from now on.
Skip validation because the template was good.
